intro: The serial protocol of protection relays. A bay controller or gateway polls each relay on an RS-485 line or an optical fiber, and the relay only answers. Each signal is named by a function type (FUN) and an information number (INF), and events carry the relay's own time.

reset.title: Reset
reset.text: The bay controller is the primary station: it speaks first, the relay only answers. It starts by resetting the relay's communication unit. The relay confirms, and its ACD bit says: I have urgent (class 1) data.

ident.title: Who are you?
ident.text: The controller asks for class 1 data. The relay answers with its identification: manufacturer, compatibility level and software.

gi.title: General interrogation
gi.text: The controller asks for the state of every signal. The relay confirms; the answers will come as class 1 data.

gidata.title: Current state
gidata.text: One class 1 request per answer. FCB flips with every new request. The last answer, type 8, says the interrogation is complete.

fault.title: Fault
fault.text: Between events the controller asks for class 2 data: measurands. A short circuit on the feeder: the relay trips its breaker, but it cannot speak first. Its next class 2 answer shows 0 A, and ACD = 1.

trip.title: Fetch the event
trip.text: ACD = 1, so the controller asks for class 1 at once. The trip arrives with the relay's time, the fault number and the time since the fault began.

frames.ident: I am made by EXAMPLE, software V2.1
frames.measurands: Currents 0 A, voltages normal, 50.01 Hz. And I have an event

start-fixed.name: Start
start-fixed.note: 0x10: a fixed-length frame, 5 bytes in all.

link.name: Link address 12
link.note: 0x0C: which relay on the line. Only relay 12 answers.

cs-var.name: Checksum
cs-var.note: The sum of every byte from C to the last data byte, modulo 256.

head-21.name: Start · length
head-21.note: 68 L L 68: start, the length twice, start again. L = 0x15 = 21 bytes, from C to the last data byte.

head-9.name: Start · length
head-9.note: L = 9 bytes, from C to the last data byte.

c-reset.name: Control 0x40
c-reset.note: PRM 1 (from the primary), FCV 0, function 0: reset of the communication unit.

c-ack-acd.name: Control 0x20
c-ack-acd.note: PRM 0 (from the relay), ACD 1, function 0: ACK. ACD = 1 says the relay has class 1 data waiting: the controller should ask for it next.

c-class1-fcb1.name: Control 0x7A
c-class1-fcb1.note: PRM 1, FCB 1, FCV 1 (FCB counts), function 10: request class 1 data.

c-class1-fcb0.name: Control 0x5A
c-class1-fcb0.note: The same request with FCB 0: FCB flips with every new request.

c-class2-fcb1.name: Control 0x7B
c-class2-fcb1.note: PRM 1, FCB 1, FCV 1, function 11: request class 2 data.

c-send-fcb0.name: Control 0x53
c-send-fcb0.note: PRM 1, FCB 0, FCV 1, function 3: send user data, confirm it.

c-data.name: Control 0x08
c-data.note: PRM 0, ACD 0, function 8: user data. No more class 1 data.

c-data-acd.name: Control 0x28
c-data-acd.note: Function 8, user data, with ACD 1: more class 1 data is waiting.

type2.name: Type 2
type2.note: A time-tagged message with relative time, used for fault indications.

cot4.name: COT 4
cot4.note: Reset of the communication unit: the reason for this message.

cot9.name: COT 9
cot9.note: Sent because of the general interrogation.

cot2.name: COT 2
cot2.note: Cyclic: measured values, sent again and again as class 2 data.

ca.name: Common address
ca.note: 12 (0x0C): the relay's ASDU address, the same as its link address here.

fun255.name: FUN 255
fun255.note: Global: for every function of the relay.

inf3.name: INF 3
inf3.note: In an identification: after a reset of the communication unit.

inf0.name: INF 0
inf0.note: The interrogation itself, not one signal.

inf148.name: INF 148
inf148.note: 0x94: IL1, IL2, IL3, VL1, VL2, VL3, P, Q and f, 2 bytes each.

col2.name: Compatibility level 2
col2.note: Follows the companion standard, without generic services.

software.name: Software
software.note: 4 bytes the manufacturer fills: "V2.1" in ASCII here.

scn.name: Scan number 33
scn.note: 0x21: the controller picks it, the answers carry it back.

scn-end.name: Scan number 33
scn-end.note: The same number as in the command: this interrogation is complete.

dpi-on.name: DPI 2
dpi-on.note: ON: protection is in service. 1 would be OFF.

time-gi.name: CP32Time2a
time-gi.note: 0x2E10 = 11792 ms: 11.792 s, 40 min (0x28), 10 h (0x0A). Every type 1 message has a time, even in a GI answer.

time-trip.name: CP32Time2a
time-trip.note: 0x1C73 = 7283 ms: 7.283 s, 41 min, 10 h. No date, no time zone.

sin-scn.name: SIN
sin-scn.note: In a GI answer, the scan number of the interrogation: 33.

sin-0.name: SIN
sin-0.note: 0: not used in a spontaneous message.

ret.name: Relative time
ret.note: 0x002B = 43 ms from the start of the fault to the trip.

fan.name: Fault number 18
fan.note: 0x0012: each fault gets the next number. It ties the fault's messages together.

voltages.name: VL1 · VL2 · VL3
voltages.note: Each value is 2 bytes, low byte first, the 3 lowest bits are flags. 0x3570 >> 3 = 1710, then 1703 and 1708. 4096 means 2.4 × rated: 1.002, 0.998 and 1.001 × rated.

a-fcb.name: FCB
a-fcb.note: Frame count bit: flips with every new request. The same FCB again asks for the last answer again.

a-fcv.name: FCV
a-fcv.note: 1: the FCB counts in this request.

a-prm0.name: PRM
a-prm0.note: 0: sent by the secondary station, the relay.

a-acd.name: ACD
a-acd.note: Access demand: 1 means the relay has class 1 data.

a-dfc.name: DFC
a-dfc.note: Data flow control: 1 would mean the relay cannot take more data now.

facts.standard: IEC 60870-5-103 (1997), with the FT 1.2 frames of IEC 60870-5-1 and -2
facts.between: Protection relay (secondary station) → bay controller, RTU or gateway (primary)
facts.transport: RS-485 or optical fiber, 9600 or 19200 bit/s, 8 data bits and even parity
facts.security: None. Keep the line inside the substation.
facts.frames: Fixed: 10 C A CS 16 · variable: 68 L L 68 C A ASDU CS 16

tips: Only the compatible range of FUN and INF is standard. Private numbers differ between vendors, even between firmware versions: work from the relay's own point list.
FCB must flip with every new request. If it does not, the relay thinks its last answer was lost and sends it again.
The relay never speaks first. If the controller does not ask for class 1 when ACD = 1, events wait in the relay's buffer, and a full buffer loses them.
Time tags have no date and no time zone. Synchronize every relay (type 6 or IRIG-B) and agree on UTC or local time.

anatomy.c-request: The control byte of a request, 0x7A, bit by bit
anatomy.c-answer: The control byte of an answer, 0x28, bit by bit

playground.file: The relay's point list, made up for this lesson. The controller needs the same list, or it cannot tell what an INF means.
playground.link: The link address: the relay's place on the line, in every frame.
playground.common: The ASDU address. Often the same as the link address.
playground.baud: Both ends must use the same speed: 9600 or 19200 bit/s.
playground.fun: FUN 160, overcurrent protection. The INF numbers below belong to it.
playground.scale: 4096 means 2.4 times the rated value. Some relays use 1.2: the controller must know which.
playground.gi: A status: sent in every general interrogation.
playground.trip: A fault indication: type 2, with relative time and fault number. Not part of the GI.
playground.measurands: Nine measured values in one ASDU, sent as class 2 data.
